paper: Morozovska et al. 2021, arXiv:2104.00598 (flexoelectric flexon domain-wall chirality)
verdict_scope: mechanism-level (1D LGD reduction); geometry-level features scoped out

open_questions.question: Does the full 3D cylindrical core-shell flexon geometry (two diffuse axial P3-domains near the cylinder ends separated by a P3~0 region, with an azimuthal XY vortex/meron core) emerge from the same Lifshitz-invariant coupling, or does it additionally require the depolarizing-field boundary conditions at the cylinder ends?
open_questions.why_heavy: Requires building the actual 3D FEM (or a self-consistent 3D finite-difference) LGD solver with a cylindrical core-shell mesh, not a 1D wall. The axial domain pair and the meron core are geometry-level features our 1D reduction cannot produce; disentangling 'Lifshitz-invariant does it' from 'ends+depolarization do it' needs the coupled 3D electrostatics.
open_questions.compute_needed: 3D FEM/FD LGD solver (FEniCS/COMSOL-style), cylindrical mesh ~10^5-10^6 DOF, self-consistent Poisson + elasticity; nuc13 CPU or uicgpu.

open_questions.question: What is the topological index of the flexon at the cylinder ends, and is it exactly +/-1/2 (meron) as the paper claims, robust to shell permittivity and cylinder aspect ratio?
open_questions.why_heavy: The +/-1/2 index is defined on the 2D azimuthal polarization field at the end caps; computing it requires the full 3D texture and a lattice/continuum winding-number integral over the end-cap disk. A 1D wall has no azimuthal structure, so this claim is entirely unaddressed here.
open_questions.compute_needed: Same 3D solver as Q1 + a Berg-Luscher / winding-number post-processor over end-cap slices.

open_questions.question: How does the FULL flexoelectric tensor F_ijkl anisotropy (not a single scalar F) reshape the domain morphology? The paper stresses that flexoelectric ANISOTROPY 'critically influences' the texture.
open_questions.why_heavy: Our 1D model collapses F_ijkl to one effective coupling F and one scalar transverse anisotropy K. Reproducing the morphology-vs-anisotropy claim needs the tensor coupling with the correct BaTiO3 F_11, F_12, F_44 components and their interplay with the gradient tensor g_ijkl in 3D.
open_questions.compute_needed: 3D solver with full F_ijkl and g_ijkl tensors; parameter sweep over F-anisotropy ratios.

open_questions.question: Can the absolute transverse polarization (in uC/cm^2) be matched to the paper, i.e. does a dimensionalized version with the real BaTiO3 material tensors and self-consistent electrostriction/electrostatics reproduce the paper's quantitative magnitudes, not just the sign/scaling?
open_questions.why_heavy: Requires the full material-parameter set (a_i(T), a_ij, a_ijk, g_ijkl, Q_ijkl, s_ijkl, F_ijkl, shell epsilon) from the paper's Table SI and a self-consistent electrostatic+elastic solve. Our dimensionless reduction deliberately does not carry absolute units.
open_questions.compute_needed: Dimensionalized 3D LGD solver + BaTiO3 Table SI parameters; convergence study.

open_questions.question: Where exactly is the Bloch-to-Ising wall transition (as a function of K/|a| and F), and does the net chiral moment saturation we observe at |F|~1 map onto a real physical saturation of the flexon chirality, or is it an artifact of the finite anisotropy K?
open_questions.why_heavy: Requires a 2-parameter (K, F) phase diagram of the 1D wall with careful separation of peak-vs-integral saturation, plus an analytic stability analysis of the Ising wall against the Lifshitz perturbation to pin the transition line from first principles rather than by scan.
open_questions.compute_needed: Dense 2D (K,F) relaxation sweep + linear stability (BdG-like) analysis of the wall; cheap, spark-local, but analytically heavy.

next_steps: Build a 3D finite-difference LGD relaxer on a cylindrical core-shell mesh with self-consistent Poisson to attempt the actual flexon geometry (closes Q1, Q2).
Extend the coupling from scalar F to the full F_ijkl tensor and sweep the anisotropy ratio to reproduce the morphology-vs-anisotropy claim (closes Q3).
Dimensionalize with BaTiO3 Table SI parameters and compare absolute uC/cm^2 magnitudes (closes Q4).
Compute the (K,F) phase diagram + analytic Ising-wall stability boundary to pin the Bloch-Ising transition and the true chirality-saturation origin (closes Q5).
Re-run extraction with real marker/nougat binaries once installed to upgrade extraction/marker.md and extraction/nougat.mmd from the pdftotext interim.
